blocks.title: Infrastructure Placement, Zones, and Device Behavior comparison
Infrastructure Placement, Zones, and Device Behavior exam shortcuts
items: The device must be in path and able to act.
Example: An IPS drops malicious traffic.
Example: An IDS receives packets from a network tap.
Example: A life-safety service must remain reachable.
Example: An admin portal becomes unavailable if control fails.
Use zones to separate exposed and internal systems.
Example: Public servers are placed in a DMZ.
blocks.example: Focus on the exact requirement in the scenario before choosing the control.

questions.q: A security appliance must continue allowing traffic if it loses power because availability is the top priority. Which failure mode is this?
questions.explanation: Fail-open allows traffic to continue when the control fails.

questions.q: A protected administrative portal must become inaccessible if its security control fails. Which failure mode is preferred?
questions.explanation: Fail-closed blocks access when the control fails.

questions.q: A security device must automatically block malicious packets. Which device attribute is required?
questions.explanation: Active devices can take action rather than only observe.

questions.q: A network sensor should observe traffic without being able to interrupt it. Which placement is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Tap/monitor placement observes a copy of traffic without sitting directly in the path.

questions.q: Public web servers are placed in a DMZ separate from internal systems. Which concept is being applied?
questions.explanation: Security zones separate systems by trust level and exposure.
